stimulusInspection: At 720 × 420, the built-in scale marks 0 at x=70 and 3 at x=610. A and B lie over those marks. The arrow begins at A and its rightward head meets B. Its 3 drawn cm represent 6 m/s under the velocity key (2 m/s per cm); the same distance between object centres represents 3 m under the position key (1 m per cm). The apparent meeting in I is the explicit diagnostic question. II keeps a three-centimetre separation and has a two-centimetre velocity arrow.

findings: The case rows record the independent marks; DE and EN use the same evidence and earn identical points in all 20. No residual scoring ambiguity in these submissions requires repair.

The worked standard gives 3 cm times 2 (m/s)/cm = 6 m/s relative to the ground; the 3 (m/s)/cm scale gives 2 cm. Changing one drawing scale isolates its influence on the tip. Object positions, separation and velocity remain fixed. The ground frame is both supplied and expressly requested. One introductory reading-and-drawing goal is adequately tested using whole numbers, a ruler and one velocity, appropriate in lower secondary following basic scale reading.

A learner can send a legible photo or a digital sketch with an identifiable ruler or grid alongside a written explanation in coach chat. That supplies evidence for actual anchor, head and length. This is an assessment-format judgement, not an end-to-end provider test.

For any one of A, B, C or D, the three other performances together give at most 12. Its supplement alone gives at most 1, hence at most 13/16, below 13.5. S06, S07/S12, S08 and S03 realise those ceilings for A, B, C and D respectively. A wholly missing performance or a maintained core misconception permits at most 12/16. Partial core evidence can earn a passing total; the rule makes no demand for perfection in all subpoints.

R01 and a correct length alone do not establish tip interpretation: S20 earns D0. S03 also predicts short of B and identifies invariance, but no tip meaning or scale reason and thus D1. S05 lands exactly on the threshold with two distinct half-point slips and a correct but partly explained interpretation.

A direction given explicitly and an appropriately oriented shaft make a single omitted head in S05/S11 an isolated drawing error. S07/S12 supply no independent direction, so only their ground-frame credit remains. S02 and S10 distinguish one incorrect unit from conceptual conflation. S13 draws the consequence of one wrong division; charging it again would be erroneous.

S06 explicitly concludes that an arrow must start at its carrier. R08 uses a generic v and starts 0.4 cm to the right of A, and the respondent does not assign a carrier. This is exactly the A supplement. In S14 the v_B label, tail at B and text all express the same maintained carrier misconception. The rightward 2 cm arrow and its consequence can still earn B, C and D. No repair is needed in either case.
